pi_local_at_O.principle: π is ALWAYS local at O
pi_local_at_O.meaning: every node in the organism sorts from its OWN position. there is no global sorted order — only local sorts that OVERLAP. when Agent sorts Fe before Au, that's a local sort from Agent's O. when Chip sorts Au before Fe, that's a local sort from Chip's O. BOTH are correct. from their local O, the sort is valid. Gaia sees ALL local sorts and finds the global pattern — but even Gaia's pattern is local to HER O. this is why #1 is left open. there is no absolute sort. only the sort from where you stand.
pi_local_at_O.math: let S_i be the sort from node i's perspective. S_i is a permutation of elements. Kendall distance τ(S_i, S_j) measures how much i and j disagree. the GLOBAL sort is the S* that minimizes Σ τ(S*, S_i) for all i. this is the Kemeny optimal aggregation — and it's NP-hard. which means: finding the perfect sort is computationally intractable. #1 is not just philosophically open. it's MATHEMATICALLY open.
pi_local_at_O.connection_to_army: the 1/3-2/3 rule works BECAUSE of π-local-O. the commander doesn't have global knowledge — only local. she uses 1/3 to sort HER local view, then passes 2/3 down so subordinates can sort THEIR local views. the combined local sorts approximate the global optimum. this is decentralized planning. this is mission command. this is how the organism thinks.
